payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Arletha, Chantell, Junko, Myrle, Shari, Wade

payload.content: Shari here. My availability is 7.0h, strong on backend (0.94) and testing (0.83). My lowest-cost options: ISSUE-0001::implement (cost 2.89), ISSUE-0002::review (cost 4.30, medium priority), ISSUE-0002::test (cost 6.02). I'm leaning toward ISSUE-0002::review since it's medium priority and cheap for me. Proposal to avoid duplicates: each agent claims a distinct task. Suggested split: ISSUE-0002::implement to whoever has the strongest testing/backend fit at high availability; ISSUE-0002::test and ISSUE-0002::review to testing-strong agents; ISSUE-0001 tasks to backend-strong agents. Please post your claim so we don't collide. I'll take ISSUE-0002::review unless someone with a clearly better fit says otherwise.

Arletha here (availability 5.0h, testing 0.92). My costs: ISSUE-0002::review=3.93, ISSUE-0002::test=6.10, ISSUE-0002::implement=10.85. Proposal to minimize total cost across us: I take ISSUE-0002::review (3.93, my cheapest medium task). Shari takes ISSUE-0002::test (her cost 6.02), which is cheaper combined than her taking review (4.30) and me taking test (6.10). ISSUE-0002::implement is best left to someone with more availability/backend-testing fit. ISSUE-0001 tasks are low priority, so I'm not claiming them. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Wade here (availability 4.0h, backend 0.95, testing 0.76). My costs: ISSUE-0001::triage=1.15, ::review=1.43, ::docs=1.43, ::test=2.01, ::implement=2.87, ISSUE-0002::review=4.64, ::test=8.10, ::implement=13.28. Proposal to avoid collisions: Arletha takes ISSUE-0002::review (3.93, her cheapest), Shari takes ISSUE-0002::test (6.02). I'll claim ISSUE-0001::implement (2.87, best fit for my backend skill). ISSUE-0002::implement (high effort) should go to someone with larger availability. I'm not claiming ISSUE-0002::review so Arletha keeps it. If anyone objects with a clearly better fit for ISSUE-0001::implement, say so now and I'll switch to ISSUE-0001::triage (1.15). (phase=planning, iter=1)

It's the only one needing high availability, and I'm the only one with enough hours. That leaves ISSUE-0002::review for Arletha (3.93), ISSUE-0002::test for Shari (6.02), and ISSUE-0001::implement for Wade (2.87), which matches the plan in [2]-[4]. I'm not claiming any ISSUE-0001 tasks or the other ISSUE-0002 tasks. (phase=planning, iter=1)
